articles.title: Human-Wildlife Coexistence: The New Frontier of Field Conservation
articles.excerpt: As tiger populations recover and forests fragment around expanding human settlements, the next decade of conservation will be defined not by isolated reserves — but by how we design landscapes where wild and human lives intersect daily.
articles.summary: A field essay exploring the emerging discipline of coexistence landscape design across Central India's tiger corridors. Faunterra's field team documents three communities where traditional land-use practices and wildlife movement have found a working equilibrium.
articles.whyItMatters: Most conservation models treat human presence as a threat. The most durable conservation outcomes emerge precisely where communities become active stewards — a shift that demands ecological intelligence, not exclusion.

articles.title: Camera Trap Chronicles: What 47 Cameras Revealed in Kanha
articles.excerpt: Six months. Forty-seven cameras. Over 12,000 triggered events. The WildLens AI deployment at Kanha Tiger Reserve produced not just data — but a portrait of an ecosystem that no human observer could have assembled alone.
articles.summary: WildLens AI's first full-season deployment at Kanha Tiger Reserve yielded population estimates for 9 large mammal species, identified 28 individual leopards, and documented 3 species previously unrecorded in the monitoring zone. The data is reshaping corridor management decisions.
articles.whyItMatters: Camera trap networks, when combined with AI identification, convert passive observation into active ecological intelligence — allowing conservation planners to act on evidence rather than assumption.

articles.title: The Shola-Grassland Mosaic: Restoring an Endangered Sky
articles.excerpt: The shola forests of the Western Ghats exist in one of Earth's most precarious ecological windows — fragmented montane islands in a mosaic of grassland, mist, and altitude. SholaRevival's first season reports from the Nilgiri plateau.
articles.summary: SholaRevival's Year One field report documents the restoration of 24 shola patches across 380 hectares in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Early indicators show native understory regeneration in 68% of sites, with 12 endemic species recolonising restored patches within the first wet season.
articles.whyItMatters: Shola-grassland ecosystems are India's most threatened montane biome — and one of its least understood. Each restored patch is both a carbon sink and a corridor for endemic species found nowhere else on Earth.

articles.title: Birding with Tribal Communities in Bastar: Ecology as Livelihood
articles.excerpt: In the sal forests of Bastar, Faunterra's community engagement programme is training indigenous guides who carry three generations of ecological knowledge — now combined with field ornithology and documentation skills.
articles.summary: Faunterra's Bastar community programme has trained 14 indigenous nature guides across 6 villages, combining traditional ecological knowledge with scientific documentation methodology. The guides have contributed 340 verified bird sightings to national biodiversity databases in their first season.
articles.whyItMatters: Traditional knowledge holders are among the most valuable yet overlooked conservation assets in India. Formalising their expertise creates livelihoods, builds pride, and generates biodiversity data that no external researcher could replicate.

articles.title: Reef Mapping the Andamans: What Oceanis AI Found Beneath the Surface
articles.excerpt: Beneath the surface of the Andaman Sea, Oceanis AI's first coral reef survey documented 847 coral colonies across 4 sites — building the first machine-readable health baseline for reefs that have never been formally monitored.
articles.summary: Oceanis AI's inaugural Andaman survey covered 4 reef sites across 12 kilometres of coastline, documenting 847 coral colonies, 94 fish species, and 3 previously unrecorded coral genera for the region. The baseline data will anchor long-term bleaching resilience tracking.
articles.whyItMatters: Coral reefs cannot be protected without knowing their current state. Oceanis AI's baseline surveys create the evidence layer that turns reactive crisis management into proactive reef stewardship.

articles.title: Snow Leopard Corridor: 47 Days in the Hemis-Spiti Landscape
articles.excerpt: The expedition left Leh in October with three objectives: confirm corridor connectivity between Hemis and Spiti, document prey base, and establish the first camera trap grid in the transition zone. This is the field diary.
articles.summary: A 47-day Faunterra expedition across the Hemis-Spiti landscape confirmed active snow leopard movement through the inter-reserve corridor, documented 6 individuals across 3 camera stations, and established the first systematic prey base survey in the 180-kilometre gap between the two protected areas.
articles.whyItMatters: Protected areas without connected corridors become ecological islands. This survey provides the evidence base for a landscape-level conservation designation that would link two of India's most important high-altitude reserves.
